summary: Count every word with `Counter`, then pick the word with the highest count, breaking ties alphabetically with one sort key. Lowercasing first makes `Hello` and `hello` the same word.

blocks.title: Import Counter
blocks.text: `Counter` counts how many times each item appears in one line of code.

blocks.title: Lowercase, split and count
blocks.text: `.lower()` before `.split()` merges different cases of the same word. `cnt` maps each word to its count, e.g. `{'the': 3, 'and': 2, …}`.

blocks.title: Highest count, then alphabetical
blocks.text: `min` with the key `(-count, word)`: the minus sign makes the biggest count the smallest key, and on a tie the word itself decides, so the alphabetically first wins. `most_common(1)` would NOT break ties alphabetically.

complexity: Time O(W) to count the words plus one pass to pick the best — instant.
pitfalls: Using `most_common(1)` — ties go to the first word seen, not the alphabetical one.
